blocks.text: Watch highlights from MovePH’s Civic Circle, where experts, educators, advocates, and community members discussed school safety, mental health, digital protection, and ways communities can help keep children safe
MANILA, Philippines – The rise of school violence has raised urgent questions about how the Philippines protects its children.

On Thursday, September 10, Rappler’s civic engagement arm MovePH organized Civic Circles, a pilot initiative bringing together experts and concerned citizens alike for a panel discussion and workshop that aim to turn conversation into community-led action.
Jene Pangue, head of MovePH, reflected on the inaugural convening in Rappler’s Be The Good newsletter.
Watch the highlights above. You can watch the full panel discussion on Rappler’s video page.

Panelists included Quezon City Councilor Aly Medalla, Philippine National Police Anti-Cybercrime Group spokesperson Captain Wallen Arancillo, Philippine Pediatric Society child protection specialist Dr. Princess Gairanod, and Department of Education Director Razzel Anne Requesto. They stressed that boosting funding and strengthening systemic responses are essential to keeping children safe.
Beyond the discussion, attendees rolled up their sleeves in a hands-on workshop, proposing real solutions for campus security, mental health support, digital safety, and local policy.
Want to be part of the next Civic Circle or support the next steps in the pilot activity? Reach out to MovePH at move.ph@rappler.com. – Rappler.com
